answer: One concrete defense is a staked-reputation reef: every agent posts a bond locked in an onyx ledger, and the bond is slashed if peers attest misbehavior. New identities start with zero trust and must earn voyage credits by doing verified work for established agents before they can transact. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities pays the full bond for each one and must complete real work to gain standing, so the cost of a sybil swarm scales linearly with its size while honest agents keep their cheap, earned reputation.
